messages.copyHint: Replace @[player number] with their in-game mention, e.g. @4.

conjurer.outcomeNote: Holding Meteor gives no daytime kill. A defended Meteor differs from a death and still has public evidence; a nighttime book attack is a separate action.

ritualist.glance: A wrong ritual guess gives no replacement role result.
ritualist.youSee: A correct Blood Ritual guess gives success feedback. A wrong guess gives no failure message and still spends an attempt; silence does not name the target’s true role.
ritualist.theySee: A successful ritual can produce its attack/death evidence. An incorrect guess does not publicly reveal your player as Ritualist.
ritualist.claimCheck: Do not fabricate an exact-role result from failure. Check eligible roles, illuminated status and the current attempt limit before acting.
ritualist.outcomeNote: A wrong role guess spends an attempt and gives no failure message. That silence is different from a correct-guess notice; it does not reveal the target’s actual role. A correct guess can still leave an Invincible target alive.

feedbackAudit.wordingCoverage: paraphrased meaning; no exact role-specific quote verified

jinx.glance: Other direct visitors can receive a private message with your name and the visited house.
jinx.youSee: You learn that you Jinxed a visitor of the chosen house. This does not give you every visitor’s player name or role, or prove the visitor died.
jinx.theySee: Direct co-visitors can see a message naming the Jinx and the shared destination. The attacked visitor is not a safe exception: a survivor can report you too. A Jinx death cause is public unless hidden by a setup effect.
jinx.claimCheck: A Crusader story cannot erase a witness’s Jinx message. A claimed Lookout list is also unsupported by simply knowing you attacked a visitor.

messages.when: At the end of a night visiting the Jinx’s chosen house
messages.text: You saw the Jinx [Jinx name] visit [target name]!
messages.copyText: You saw the Jinx @[Jinx player number] visit @[target player number]!
messages.copyHint: Replace both @ placeholders with the Jinx and destination players’ in-game mentions, e.g. @4.

messages.when: A player dies to the Jinx attack, if the cause is not hidden
messages.text: They were killed by a Jinx.

jinx.outcomeNote: No visitor-attack feedback is not an empty named visitor list. Attack feedback without a Jinx death can leave a surviving witness who knows your identity.

dreamweaver.glance: The target can see Dreamweaver/Insomnia effects, while you do not receive their exact Town role.
dreamweaver.youSee: Dreamwoven/Insomnia icons on the target’s name bar show the applied state. A cured Dreamweave loses its icon without becoming Insomnia; immune targets do not get the Dreamwoven icon.
dreamweaver.theySee: A qualifying target can see Dreamweave/Insomnia notices; a Town visit on the following night can prevent Insomnia. Insomnia and its removal change their available abilities.
dreamweaver.claimCheck: An ordinary protection story can conflict with the target’s status. Record cures and cleared effects; do not treat every applied status as permanent.
dreamweaver.outcomeNote: A selected target is not confirmed Insomnia. A qualifying Town visit on the following night can cure Dreamweave before Insomnia; prevention and later recovery are separate states.

feedbackAudit.wordingCoverage: paraphrased meaning; no exact role-specific quote verified

enchanter.glance: Your altered death information is what the public can read, not proof it was genuine.
enchanter.youSee: Your selected Enchant/Alterate is not an investigation. After an altered death, informed Coven can see the real role, while the forged will replaces the original.
enchanter.theySee: Investigatives can see altered appearances, and the graveyard can show a forged role/will. That is different from the target receiving an explicit Enchant notice.
enchanter.claimCheck: Do not cite your own frame or forged will as independent confirmation. A corpse-user or other private result may contradict the public display.
enchanter.outcomeNote: A quiet Enchant supplies no true-role reveal. Alterate only changes death information if the player dies while it applies; an unused-looking result does not justify inventing a death.

illusionist.glance: A disguised death can show a chosen role; favorable investigation is not a faction change.
illusionist.youSee: Track the chosen Illusion, Phantasm or death Disguise separately. The role-changing display does not grant the claimed role’s actual abilities.
illusionist.theySee: Investigatives can receive altered appearances, and public death information can show a Disguise. These displays do not establish the player’s actual faction.
illusionist.claimCheck: A book attack is direct and replaces the ordinary protective choice. A nonvisiting cover must account for that switch in observed movement.
illusionist.outcomeNote: Illusion changes appearances, not real abilities. A quiet night gives no new Town investigation; Phantasm and death Disguise are separate modes. Do not claim every investigator is fooled.

medusa.glance: The graveyard can hide role and will; Coven can still receive the real information.
medusa.youSee: Your Stone marks and charges track actual placements. You start passively Stoned yourself. A marked death can expose the true role/will privately to Coven while others see hidden information.
medusa.theySee: Stone is a persistent mark, not a protection notice. When a marked player dies, ordinary opponents can be denied the role and will; observers can still see a direct Stone visit.
medusa.claimCheck: A Cleric claim cannot explain a visible N1 protective visit during Grace Period. Privately readable Stoned information is not a Psychic or Sheriff result.
medusa.outcomeNote: Stone is a persistent mark, not a kill/save result. Holding makes no ordinary Stone visit. During Grace Period N1, a visible Stone visit cannot support an unavailable TP visit.

necromancer.glance: Recipients can see the corpse ability’s effect; that does not certify a Town corpse-user.
necromancer.youSee: The reanimated body can supply role-specific feedback. Record the body, destination and mode; a book attack is a separate action choice.
necromancer.theySee: Targets may receive the reanimated ability’s normal message or attack evidence. They do not thereby learn that a Town Retributionist produced it.
necromancer.claimCheck: A Ret cover has a smaller legal body pool. Evil/hidden bodies or private self-protection can expose a false Town-only corpse history.
necromancer.outcomeNote: An unusable or contested corpse is not a successful result. You are roleblock-immune, but corpse availability, ability restrictions and destination failures still matter.

poisoner.glance: Drink and Smog give different visible problems to affected players.
poisoner.youSee: Record Drink versus Smog and the action’s actual outcome. A Smog rejection is not a complete list of visitor identities.
poisoner.theySee: A Drink recipient can receive roleblock/immunity feedback. Eligible visitors encountering Smog can receive an obstacle; the resident need not get that same visitor message.
poisoner.claimCheck: Match the effect witnesses describe. A roleblock or obstacle complaint is not ordinary protection feedback; Hangover and immunity can also explain failures.
poisoner.outcomeNote: No Smog rejection reported is not proof of an empty house. Drink is a separate roleblock mode. You are roleblock-immune; Smog and a book attack cannot be used together.

potion-master.glance: A Reveal gives you a private exact-role line; a Barrier recipient sees protection, not your identity.
potion-master.youSee: Reveal gives the target’s exact role; Heal can give target-attack feedback; a book attack has attack feedback. Keep the selected potion and failures separate.
potion-master.theySee: An attacked Heal recipient can receive a generic Barrier notice. Your Reveal result belongs to you/informed allies, not the investigated target.
potion-master.claimCheck: Do not present a private exact-role Reveal as a Sheriff/Seer result. A Barrier message alone does not uniquely prove Cleric or Oracle.
potion-master.outcomeNote: A quiet Heal is not save feedback. Self Heal uses the same protection mode, cannot be used in a 1v1, and is not a visit to another player. Reveal is a role result, not a visitor list.

voodoo-master.glance: Silence, Deafen and Blind affect different parts of the recipient’s screen.
voodoo-master.youSee: Record the selected thread and actual outcome. The victim’s missing chat/results are not an exact-role result for you.
voodoo-master.theySee: Silence prevents speech, Deafen removes other players’ chat/whispers, and Blind suppresses nightly results. On an ordinary text-chat trial, a Silenced player can use the limited ellipsis response.
voodoo-master.claimCheck: A protection cover can conflict with the recipient’s status. Blind notification wording is inconsistent across references; do not promise a particular explanatory line.

messages.when: Silence takes effect / the player attempts to speak
messages.text: Your voice seems to be lost! You can't speak.

voodoo-master.outcomeNote: Silence, Deafen and Blind suppress different things. No victim report does not establish failure. Sources disagree on a Blind notice, so no exact Blind line is promised.

wildling.glance: Your private movement and whisper information is not automatically public.
wildling.youSee: Sensed travel and permitted whisper information can give real destinations or private conversations. Keep what you actually observed distinct from a complete role reveal.
wildling.theySee: Observed players do not receive your entire private log. Your direct Sense/book visit can still be visible to other observers.
wildling.claimCheck: Tracker/Lookout reporting must match what that Town role could see. Do not copy private whispers or unrelated movement into a public claimed result.
wildling.outcomeNote: An empty travel result can hide astral movement. Sense is not an exact-role reveal or Spy-style effect log; public whispers you hear are separate from the nightly travel report.

covenite.theySee: A book target may receive Coven attack feedback. Other players do not receive a special Covenite investigation/protection result.
covenite.claimCheck: Separate no-book holds from book travel. An invented nightly investigation is not supplied by Covenite’s actual ability.
covenite.outcomeNote: Without the book, a quiet night is normal and creates no Covenite action result. With the book, distinguish an attack attempt from an actual death.

cultist.theySee: The converted player receives the new faction/team context and keeps their role’s real ability. Earlier Town demonstrations can remain mechanically genuine.
cultist.claimCheck: A former Town confirmation does not prove current allegiance. Do not claim Indoctrinate itself was a Town investigation or a role swap.

baker.glance: A public Famine announcement identifies the transformation, not the player who transformed.
baker.youSee: Bread markers and living recipients track your progress. Your starting Bread is separate from the ordinary living recipients needed for transformation.
baker.theySee: Transformation announces Famine to the town. Bread/Starvation effects are different from an ordinary protective save; the announcement alone does not name your player.
baker.claimCheck: Do not turn Bread status into a Cleric save or a visitor report. After transformation, your history must switch from Feed to Famine’s current ability.
baker.outcomeNote: Starting Bread is not a new Feed. A failed Feed adds no new recipient. Bread is not protection, and transformation/deaths must be separated from earlier feeding visits.

berserker.glance: Rampage feedback and public deaths are not a complete visitor list.

berserker.theySee: Victims can get attack/death feedback and public deaths show the relevant cause unless hidden. A War transformation is publicly announced.
berserker.claimCheck: Do not report kill progress as an investigative check. Once War arrives, follow its new two-target action rather than the earlier Berserker story.
berserker.outcomeNote: Early restricted nights or a held attack do not produce kills. Track actual kills and rampage victims separately; transformation needs the real threshold, not merely selected targets.

plaguebearer.glance: Your infection markers are broader than a list of visitors to one house.
plaguebearer.youSee: Your infection display and spread information track Plague contacts. Distinguish fresh spread from starting infections and contacts already infected.
plaguebearer.theySee: Ordinary infected players do not receive your infection map. The eventual Pestilence announcement is public, but does not reveal which numbered player transformed.
plaguebearer.claimCheck: If using a movement cover, distinguish active Infect, passive spread and existing infection. An infection event alone does not assign a visitor to a numbered house.

soul-collector.glance: Your soul count is private; becoming Death is publicly announced.
soul-collector.youSee: You gain a passive soul each night and extra souls when Reaped players die. Reap frames their apparent faction; placing it does not itself kill them or immediately award an extra soul.
soul-collector.theySee: Investigatives can see the altered appearance of a Reaped player. At the threshold, the public Death transformation gives the town urgent new information.
soul-collector.claimCheck: An astral Reap does not support a normal visiting cover. Keep private soul counts and invented exact-role findings out of public Town reports.
soul-collector.outcomeNote: A quiet Reap is not a kill. A soul can come from the role’s permitted passive/death conditions; do not claim every Reap immediately awards one or gives a Town result.

doomsayer.glance: Your success/failure line is private; a wrong set does not reveal which guess was wrong.
doomsayer.youSee: A correct set of three guesses produces success feedback. A failed set says at least one was wrong, without supplying a replacement list of roles.
doomsayer.theySee: A successful Doom creates the relevant deaths and your departure/win evidence. Other players do not get a routine list of your failed guesses.
doomsayer.claimCheck: Do not treat one failed triple as three cleared players. Keep the permitted guess categories and the actual night’s outcome separate.

messages.when: All three submitted role guesses are correct
messages.text: You have chosen wisely. All three roles are correct.

messages.when: At least one submitted role guess is wrong
messages.text: You have chosen poorly. At least one of your guesses is incorrect.

doomsayer.outcomeNote: A failed set means at least one guess is wrong; it does not identify which. Do not replace a failure with three negative role checks. Doom is not defeated by an ordinary roleblock/control story.

executioner.glance: A qualifying target execution produces public outcome evidence; private target assignment is yours.
executioner.youSee: Your assigned target and actual win/transform state establish progress. A death by another route is not automatically the qualifying execution.
executioner.theySee: The trial and any revenge/win/departure events can be seen publicly. They do not give other players your earlier private target-selection information.
executioner.claimCheck: A cover story must fit the public trial. If you become Jester, switch to Jester’s conditions instead of claiming the old target objective is still active.
executioner.outcomeNote: A non-trial target death changes you into Jester privately. It is not an Executioner win or a public Jester revenge event; update the role and its later requirements.

jester.glance: The public revenge announcement can distinguish a qualifying hanging from an invalid one.
jester.youSee: The interface gives a daily Chatterbox requirement and progress. A qualifying execution and available Haunt are different from failing the quota or dying at night.
jester.theySee: The town sees the hanging and the appropriate revenge/no-revenge announcement. A later Haunt creates attack/death evidence.
jester.claimCheck: A role claim does not replace the quota or qualifying death condition. Preserve which voters and targets the client actually permits.

messages.when: A Jester without a completed Chatterbox is hanged
messages.text: The Jester cannot be bothered getting revenge beyond the grave!

pirate.glance: Scour information concerns your Landlubbers; it is not a normal Sheriff result.
pirate.youSee: Your objective and Scour feedback concern the three Landlubbers. A Plunder is a separate attack action with limited charges and a real outcome.
pirate.theySee: A victim can receive Pirate attack/death feedback; public deaths can advance the objective even when you did not kill that player.
pirate.claimCheck: Use the current Scour/Plunder rules. Old duel choices and duel-result messages are not a valid current claim history.
pirate.outcomeNote: Scour is a Landlubber check; Plunder is a separate attack. A failed attack is not a negative Scour, and a Landlubber dying to another cause can still advance the objective. No old duels.

arsonist.glance: Most victims do not get a routine Doused notice; another Arsonist can detect their own gasoline.
arsonist.youSee: Track active Douse, passive Douse from visitors and self-Doused state separately. Taking no action can Clean you; Ignite is a distinct action.
arsonist.theySee: A normal Douse is not a protection/save notice. Fire deaths create public evidence later, while observers may see direct Douse travel.
arsonist.claimCheck: A visiting cover can fit a direct Douse destination but has no real protection. Clean/astral Ignite can fit a nonvisiting story only if earlier observed travel also agrees.
arsonist.outcomeNote: A quiet Douse gives no Cleric save feedback. Clean stays home; Ignite is astral. Being Doused by another Arsonist and passive Dousing visitors are separate from a direct Douse destination.

serial-killer.glance: Roleblock retaliation can leave a different death explanation from your selected attack.
serial-killer.youSee: Your selected attack, Cautious setting and any passive retaliation are separate. Attack feedback is not an exact-role investigation.
serial-killer.theySee: Targets can get attack/death feedback. An uncautious roleblock retaliation can leave the distinctive roleblocker/jailed-SK explanation and affect their will.
serial-killer.claimCheck: Do not claim a clean ordinary visit account while ignoring retaliation. The person you chose to attack is not necessarily the only relevant victim.

serial-killer.outcomeNote: Cautious changes roleblock retaliation, not your target’s identity. Attack feedback without a death can mean defense; an uncautious retaliatory death is not an ordinary selected-target kill.

shroud.glance: A shrouded player can appear to have attacked; death evidence alone does not identify their intent.
shroud.youSee: Record direct Attack versus Shroud and the action’s outcome. A failed shrouding route can result in a different direct attack path.
shroud.theySee: The forced attack can create Murder evidence on the shrouded player. The attacked recipient and public deaths can supply attack evidence without establishing a willing killer.
shroud.claimCheck: Keep your own destination and the forced attacker’s destination separate. A Seer/Tracker account must fit the movement it actually claims to observe.
shroud.outcomeNote: A shrouded player staying home can redirect the outcome to an attack on that player. A shrouded visit is not proof of a willing attack; preserve mode and actual destination feedback.

werewolf.glance: A persistent Scent result does not mean you visited that player again tonight.
werewolf.youSee: Scent and Full Moon attacks give different information. An existing scent can keep supplying destinations without a fresh visit to that subject.
werewolf.theySee: Victims of a Full Moon attack/rampage can get attack feedback and leave public deaths. That does not broadcast your complete private scent history.
werewolf.claimCheck: A fresh Tracker account about an old scented player can conflict with your real attack elsewhere. Preserve the current moon and actual travel mode.
werewolf.outcomeNote: Non-Full Moon Scent is not an attack. Existing scents can still report when you are jailed. Staying home on a Full Moon can rampage at home; do not invent an outward visit.

cursed-soul.glance: A successful role swap changes both role cards; it does not swap factions.
cursed-soul.youSee: A successful Soul Swap changes your role card and controls. Your faction remains the same; an attempted swap does not prove the chosen role was acquired.
cursed-soul.theySee: The other player can see their changed role, while keeping their faction. A later Wandering Souls victory/departure is a separate public event.
cursed-soul.claimCheck: Do not keep reporting the old role’s power after losing it. An old role read does not establish anyone’s current role or faction.

vampire.glance: A converted Town player keeps their real role ability and sees a new faction context.

vampire.claimCheck: A genuine Town-role demonstration can remain genuine after conversion. Avoid the obsolete youngest-biter account and distinguish conversion from a kill.

pestilence.theySee: The public transformation announces Pestilence. Affected players can experience stack effects and lethal outcomes; this is not a standard protection message.
